name: Crary Science and Engineering Center
description: CSEC is a scientific research facility with offices, storage, library, an aquarium, and laboratories for biology, atmospheric science and    earth science research.  The building is configured in three "phases" at different elevations connected by a walkway spine.  A dedicated    1,900 foot pipeline supplies seawater to the building's aquarium from the station seawater intake well.
aeds: Mounted in Phase 1 near Manager's Office

name: CSEC Emergency GENSE
description: Houses a 400kW Caterpillar diesel-engine generator connected to the CSEC (Building 1) to provide emergency back-up power.    Building 2 also supplies power to Building 1's emergency lighting, air handling units, heat exchangers, boilers, walk-in freezers,    and environmental rooms. It is a single-room building with one personnel door and one overhead roll-up door.  A 2-ton trolley    crane is provided on an overhead monorail.

name: Core Storage
description: Provides refrigerated storage at McMurdo Station and supplements the refrigerated storage capacity of Building 001, CSEC. It currently    does not provide freezer space, but an addition planned for construction during the 1999 winter will add the capacity for    freezer storage space. Building 003 is an insulated building with a gabled roof located near Building 001. It is composed of three areas,    the entryway/foyer, refrigerated room, and attic space with mechanical room.

name: Science Support Center
description: Two-story multi-department building. The top floor of the SSC houses the Field Training classroom, offices, kitchen, two bathrooms and the Search And Rescue HQ. The second floor 'back bay' includes additional storage space for Field Science Support equipment and a snow machine instruction area. This area is designated as McMurdo Stations backup MCI casualty collection facility. The Mechanical Equipment Center (MEC) located on the bottom floor is used for the maintenance and repair of mechanical equipment such as snow machines, generators and 2-stroke power tools. The first floor contains a full-featured shop, storage rooms, a janitor closet and two restrooms.

name: Chapel of the Snows
description: Single-story structure with a center high-bay nave flanked by offices on one side and by storage and furnace rooms on the other. Used    as a non-denominational chapel and NSFA chaplain's office.

name: Field Safety Training Ops Building
description: Originally constructed as an earth sciences and glaciology laboratory, for which it was used until 1992. Converted in 1995 for use a field training safety office and classroom. Partitioned into eight offices and storage rooms and a furnace room. Building 139 was constructed as an addition to the building in 1965, and houses two walk-in freezers used for the storage of ice cores and other scientific samples. There    is also a small attic space used for storage.

name: Field Safety Training Ops Building
description: Originally constructed as an earth sciences and glaciology laboratory, for which it was used until 1992. Converted in 1995 for use a field training safety office and classroom. Building 139 was constructed as an addition to the building in 1965, and houses two walk-in freezers used for the storage of ice cores and other scientific samples. There    is also a small attic space used for storage.

name: MCC - Post Office - Central Supply
description: Movement Control Center (MCC), logistics offices and warehousing for Central Supply. Building 140 consists of an existing two-story warehouse remodeled for office, warehouse and assembly use, with high-bay warehouse addition. The building serves as a logistics office, office supply warehouse, aircraft passenger processing center, and special cargo handling facility.    The cargo handlding facility is has a precast concrete slab floor.

name: Fuel Department
description: Two-story warehouse-type building used primarily as office, shop and storage space for the fuels work center. The first floor includes offices, a shop, and a large open storage area.  The open second floor is used for the storage of electrical inventory.

name: Medical Clinic
description: Single story building used as a level 3 trauma medical facility. The building is equipped with a dedicated emergency generator.

name: Vehicle Maintenance Facility (VMF)
description: Single-story facility used for the maintenance and repair of all vehicles. A high-bay area includes nine repair bays, a welding bay, battery storage room and oil dispensing room.  A low-bay area includes offices, a lounge, machine shop, engine repair shop, parts storage, tool storage, restrooms and a boiler room.
aeds: Mounted on wall between Tool Room and Parts Room.

name: Dive Shack
description: Single-story building used as a dive locker. Includes areas for equipment storage, cleaning and maintenance, toilet facilities, and a breathing air compressor.

name: Thiele Gravity Survey Hut
description: Previously housed a 20 hp pump used to transfer water from the new water plant (Building 198) to tanks in Building 126, the old water plant. The equipment was removed during the 98-99 summer season.

name: Greenhouse (Hydroponics Lab)
description: Single-story building assembled in 1988-89 out of discarded Williams Field portable buildings. Used as a hydroponics greenhouse.

name: Pass Pump House
description: Single-story building used to house two 50-hp pumps used to transfer fuel to Williams Field.  The building is divided into a pump    room and a control room.

name: Fire Pump House (Dorms)
description: Single-story building used as a pump house for the automatic fire sprinkler systems in Dormitories 201, 202, and 206 through 211.  Includes a 10,000 gallon water storage tank and a 750 gpm, diesel-powered fire pump.

name: Building 155: Station Core Facility
description: Two-story building divided into a single-story "subsistence" area and a two-story dormitory area. The subsistence area houses the station dining facility, laundry, NSFA photo labs, and boiler room. The dormitory area includes dormitory rooms housing up to six persons each, television and radio studios, a store, a barber shop, and offices.
aeds: Highway One, across from Barber Shop
Galley, mounted in kitchen area near doors exiting to hot food line

The building is used as a warehouse for VXE-6 aircraft parts, weather balloon equipment, and general materials. The second floor is used for DNF grantee staging and storage.

name: Supply - Cold Storage
description: Building is a two-story, prefabricated, steel structure with uninsulated metal siding. The building is used as a warehouse for aircraft    parts and materials.

name: Berg Field Center
description: Two-story building used for the storage, maintenance, and repair of science field camp equipment such as tents, stoves, and sleds. The first    floor contains storage rooms, a restroom, and a storage room for survival bags and other helicopter support items. The second floor includes    additional warehouse space, a kitchen and lounge, and an office.

name: Carpentry Shop
description: Single-room building used in conjunction with Building 191/191A as a carpentry shop.

name: BFC Freezer (Walk-In)

name: Frozen Food Storage
description: Single-story, prefabricated, metal structure. The building has no interior partitions. The building functions as a frozen food storage warehouse with six air conditioning units. One heated office is located on the dock. It also provides warm storage for the electric forklift.

name: Administration, Central Comms, SFA, NPP
description: Communnications and Central Comms Offices. Two-story, steel frame structure with insulated metal panels.  Interior partitions are a combination of wood and steel framing with wood paneling and/or gypsum board. The building functions as the NSFA main administration offices.

name: NSF Dorm (Hotel California)
description: Two-story dormitory used primarily to house NSF grantees and personnel travelling through McMurdo Station to other locations. The first floor includes 13 two-person rooms, a laundry room, a women's bathroom, a sauna, and a mechanical room. The second floor includes 8 two-person rooms, a bunkroom, a lounge, and men's bathroom. Originally constructed in 1968, the building interior was completely rehabilitated in 1986.

name: Chalet (NSF Offices)
description: A-frame style building containing offices for senior NSF and contractor personnel. The building containsfive offices, a storage room, a restroom, a mechanical room, and a central assembly room with a conference mezzanine area above.

name: Auto Storage
description: Two-story warehouse used for the unheated storage of automotive parts.

name: Hazardous Waste Facility
description: This facility was constructed in the 97-98 summer season. It is used for waste sorting, office space for hazardous waste personnel, and radioactive material handling. The main portion of the building was built using the steel from the old pumphouse that was located at Hut Point. The building is located in the hazardous waste yard.
aeds: Haz Waste, mounted next to the door to the Rad space

name: Flammable Storage
description: Building is used as a warehouse for the storage of safety equipment and various flammable materials, including flammable and combustible liquids.

name: FEMC - IT - NSF Offices

name: Dry Foods Storage

name: Paint Barn - Storage
description: Used for small-quantity paint storage and painting work. Serves as Facilities Maintenance and Construction painting work center. Building is a single-room T-5 with a smaller shed-roof T-5 attached.

name: Seawater Intake
description: Single-story, single-room building used as a shelter over a seawater intake well.  The building is located at the end of a man-made earthen jetty extending approximately 150 feet into McMurdo Sound from the shoreline. The building also houses two submersible seawater pumps for the Building 001, Phase III, aquarium and two pumps for the Building 187, the old aquarium.

name: Sewage Masticator

name: Firehouse - Telephone Exchange
